question: Identify a promising result outside the submitted bit-PHP paper and test whether it answers an explicitly posed open problem.

sources.title: On Zeros of a Polynomial in a Finite Grid
sources.read_scope: Theorem 6.1(c), Conjecture 6.3 and Remark 6.4, section 7.4 open multiplicity question
sources.comparison: The constant-coefficient endpoint is classical. The explicit questions concern possibly infinite grids over rings or multiplicities, not the finite encoded positive-coefficient-degree frontier.

sources.title: Subspace coverings with multiplicities
sources.read_scope: Introduction, Theorem 1.1 comparison, concluding finite-field and large-multiplicity questions
sources.comparison: Repeated geometric covering and vanishing multiplicities impose information absent from a reduced finite-state selector identity. No reduction to our factor-count theorem was established.

sources.title: Covering Symmetric Sets of the Boolean Cube by Affine Hyperplanes
sources.read_scope: Abstract, Problem 2 and scope of Theorems 3-5, Open Problem 11
sources.comparison: The remaining question concerns affine covers of arbitrary weight-determined subsets of larger grids in characteristic zero. Our result fixes a punctured product and uses degree-limited coefficients in finite-field state indicators.

verdict: Promising exact independent candidate with unknown novelty; no explicitly posed open problem solved by its exact scope was identified. This is a bounded search, not an exhaustive priority assessment or fresh correctness verification.
